chapters.title: A Swedish activewear brand on a headless storefront
chapters.caption: strongerlabel.com in September, before the first test went live.
text: Stronger sells activewear from Stockholm on a Centra and React Router storefront, with content in Storyblok. I joined through TRY in September as the frontend between the brand's e-commerce team and the dev agency that runs the storefront.

chapters.title: The ask was a view counter
chapters.caption: The product page already carried four earlier test winners; the view counter would have been the fifth element competing for the same screen.
text: The brief that reached me was small: improve the "people browsing" pill on the product page, a widget that had won an earlier test. The test history said why not. Ten experiments, nine of them on the product page, four winners stacked on the same screen. The product list, the size picker and the mini-cart had never been tested.

I asked for two weeks to find out where the next test should go. Walking the store as a shopper next to Gymshark, AYBL and Aim'n gave four gaps: no delivery promise under the buy button, sold-out sizes as a dead end, no bestseller signal on the product list, and discounted kits whose saving only showed on the kit's own page. Each gap became a test with one hypothesis, one primary metric and an exposure point that only counts shoppers who could see the change.

chapters.title: The bestseller badge, first out
chapters.caption: Figma, ships state. The badge takes the Archive badge's slot in the card's top corner, so the grid never shifts. Goal: add to cart, target +5 %.
text: The product list had no signal for what sells. Shoppers chose between forty near-identical tights with nothing but price to go on. The badge reuses the slot the Archive badge already had in the card's top corner, so the grid never shifts, and it follows the colour variant rather than the product family.

It looked like a one-day job until I traced where the flag lived: the product page reads a Centra attribute, the list cards read Voyado Elevate, so a feed mapping came first. Goal add to cart, target +5 %.

chapters.title: The badge went live on 20 October
chapters.caption: Control and variant from production, same session. Badge style GT America 500 12/15 on #18181b.
text: "Bästsäljare" on the product-list cards, 50/50 on a user cookie, GA4 in BigQuery, Bayesian with CUPED and a product-list view as activation metric. Nine days in, 64,222 users: bestseller card clicks 22.5 % → 23.1 % (+2.7 %, 96 % chance to beat control), PLP → PDP click 48.7 % → 49.4 % (+1.2 %), the other cards +1.0 %. Add to cart 14.7 % → 14.6 %, purchase 3.91 % → 3.86 %, both flat.
The click lift looked like a win by day two; the goal is still flat, so it runs the full two weeks. Final read 3 November.

chapters.title: Accessibility fixes along the way
chapters.caption: Header and cart drawer by keyboard: focus goes in, stays in, and comes back out.
text: Between tests, the storefront got the accessibility work it had been missing: keyboard reach of the header and the cart, focus handling in the cart drawer, and the gaps that still remain, documented so they can be closed.

chapters.title: The five tests, designed before a line was written

tests.label: Bestseller badge
tests.title: Bestseller badge on the product list
tests.status: Live since 20 Oct · final read 3 Nov
text: The product list had no signal for what sells. The badge reuses the slot the Archive badge already had in the card's top corner, so the grid never shifts, and follows the colour variant rather than the product family.
tests.caption: Figma, ships state: mobile card, laptop card, 2-col grid.
tests.hypothesis: A bestseller badge is proof of trust, especially for someone buying their first tights. More clicks on the badged cards would lead to more adds to cart and a higher conversion, at the cost of stealing clicks from the other cards. A trade-off I was prepared to pay.
tests.metric: Add to cart rate, target +5 % relative. PLP → PDP click-through as the leading indicator; purchase and revenue guarded.
tests.result: 9 days in, 64,222 users. Bestseller card click 22.5 % → 23.1 % (+2.7 %, 96 % chance to beat control). PLP → PDP click 48.7 % → 49.4 % (+1.2 %). The other cards gained clicks too (+1.0 %), so the badge did not cannibalise. Add to cart 14.7 % → 14.6 % (−1.1 %, 29 %). Purchase 3.91 % → 3.86 %, flat.
tests.decision: Still running. Final read 3 Nov: the leading signal is there, the add-to-cart lift is not yet.

tests.label: Delivery promise
tests.title: One delivery promise, four states
tests.status: Ready · waiting on ops for the cut-off
text: Nothing under the buy button said when an order would ship. One line answers it, and because every state was a component variant, the weekend, holiday and after-cut-off copy surfaced in review before anyone built it. Ready, waiting on ops to confirm the cut-off.
tests.caption: Figma, ships state. "Beställ före 13:50 så skickas din order idag" under the buy button; after cut-off, weekend and holiday copy as component variants. Cut-off time lives in Storyblok.

tests.label: Sold-out row
tests.title: A row instead of a dead end
tests.status: Designed · exposes on a sold-out tap
text: A sold-out size was a dead end: a notify-me drawer and nothing else, even when the same tights existed in three other colours in that size. The first design redesigned the drawer. In review it shrank to one quiet row under the sizes, shown only when a sold-out size is tapped, which is also the exposure point.
tests.caption: Figma, ships state. "S är slut i Magenta · finns i" plus the sibling colours that have the size in stock. The notify-me drawer stays exactly as today.

tests.label: Similar product
tests.title: One similar product, in your size
text: The same dead end, second answer: when the size is gone in every colour, show one product that has it. Three cards became one. The card is the one that already won a bundle test, and the mapping is hand-picked, so the test measures the idea and not a recommendation engine.
tests.caption: Figma, ships state. One size-matched card with "Lägg till S", reusing the card that won the bundle test. Hand-picked map before any recommendation engine.

tests.label: Kit upgrade
tests.title: Upgrade to the kit, in the cart
text: Forty-seven discounted kits, and the saving only showed on the kit's own page. A shopper with one kit piece in the cart never learned that two more pieces made a kit and saved 248 SEK. The block sits under the matching line, the button is disabled until every size is picked, and one tap swaps the line for the kit.
tests.caption: Figma, variant with sizes picked. The missing pieces under the cart line with one swap button; six changes came out of an adversarial review. Primary metric: revenue per exposed user.
